key_insight: An exponentially weighted ensemble of five deep learning models improved lung adenocarcinoma histologic growth pattern classification from H&E whole-slide images.
clinical_relevance: More accurate pattern classification in digital pathology may support better prognostic assessment and treatment planning for lung adenocarcinoma.
method: Built an ensemble from EfficientNet-B3, DeiT3, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and ConvNeXt.
Assigned model weights using a softmax transform of each model’s Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) score.
Evaluated performance with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on 25,545 image patches from the Dartmouth-Hitchcock dataset.
evidence_signal: The ensemble reached 96.52% accuracy and Cohen’s kappa of 0.9648, outperforming the best single model with a statistically significant gain and bootstrap confidence interval support.
watch_item: Performance was measured on a single dataset and patch-based evaluation, so external validation and slide-level clinical testing are still needed.
paper_title: Exponentially weighted ensemble deep learning for histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma
